I will keep to the cropping pattern I trust most here: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. In Quzhou County, that rotation fits my weather, my soil, and the way I know how to farm. I do not have formal schooling, so I will not gamble on a complicated crop that needs more market judgment or special management. Wheat and maize are familiar, the seed and fertilizer are easy for me to buy, and I know the work rhythm well. At the start of the season, I will focus on managing the wheat that is already in the field with topdressing, watering, and weed and disease control when needed. After harvest, I will quickly sow summer maize, use improved or hybrid seed, give enough fertilizer for steady growth, irrigate when the rain is short, and spray only as much as needed to keep pests under control. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical and matches the way I would prepare land with ordinary local machinery.
